newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi SABIC starts operations at petchem plant.
newsitem.headline: Saudi SABIC starts operations at petchem plant.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries said on Saturday production had begun at a $360 million Saudi-Taiwanese petrochemicals joint venture.

The 150,000-tonnes a year 2-ethylhexanol (2-EH) plant began commercial production on October 1 after trial runs, SABIC Vice-Chairman Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Salameh said in a statement issued by the company's headquarters in Riyadh.

The first shipment of di-octyle phthalate (DOP) from a 50,000-tonne a year plant left the industrial city of Jubail on the Gulf coast on October 20. SABIC Marketing Ltd. has marketed 400 tonnes of DOP from the factory, which became operational in September.
Ethylhexanol is the main feedstock required to produce DOP, a major plasticiser component used in the manufacture of wires, cables, sheets, floor coverings and coated fabrics.
The al-Jubail Fertiliser Company (SAMAD), formed in 1979, is a 50-50 venture between Sabic and state-owned Taiwan Fertiliser Company. It came on stream in 1983, producing urea.
Bin Salameh said 2-EH and the DOP production, the company's first major product diversification, were the first of its kind in the region.

"These projects further strengthen SABIC's position as a regional industrial power and promoter of downstream industrialisation," he said. "They also reinforce our role in earning export revenues and in contributing to import substitution."
SAMAD was the first major joint venture between Saudi Arabia and Taiwan since Riyadh switched diplomatic recognition to communist China from Taiwan in 1990.
